A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, appendices, tables, figures, and equations are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classifier evaluations, crowdsourced annotation results, engagement analyses, and classification of 150,000 unseen YouTube comments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline evaluations, annotation analyses, manual prediction auditing, and a Reddit study.

M1.justification: The two-stage video filtering, human–LLM seed annotation, certainty and margin sampling, and LoRA classifier fine-tuning remain unchanged. The additional models trained on LGBTQ+ and non-LGBTQ+ annotations apply the existing procedure to different label subsets; they do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 extends the YouTube study to 45,000 Reddit comments from r/politics, r/republican, and r/democrat covering 2016–2024. Appendix K also adds evaluated YouTube coverage of gun-related, climate, abortion, and immigration topics. These expand the represented platforms and subject matter.

E2.justification: Section 4 and Table A1 add DistilBERT-SST2, Detoxify-toxic-bert, cardiffnlp hate-roBERTa, and GPT-4o comment classification comparisons. Section 5.2 also introduces pretrained Llama as a comparator in the political-model agreement audit. The existing Llama, Mistral, and GPT-4o-mini comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce binary label mappings and exclusion of neutral/irrelevant comments for the sentiment comparison, additional same-party annotation pairs across 30 batches, and a shared-comment subset for identity-specific models. Table A9 adds minimum comment-count criteria for selecting extreme videos. The original 250-instance evaluation set, reported 80/20 split, and five-epoch schedule remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds within-party agreement analysis, pretrained-versus-fine-tuned agreement, identity-conditioned annotation/model analyses, and manual inspection of 100 predicted-positive comments. Appendices K–M add controversial-topic comparisons, extreme-video case studies, and lexical analyses. The original two-example error analysis is retained in Appendix N rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Table 3 replaces mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting with bare scores while retaining its five-independent-runs caption; fewer runs are therefore not established. Section 5.2 and Table A17 introduce two-proportion z-tests and p-values. Existing confidence intervals for YouTube label distributions remain unchanged in Table A19.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces fine-tuned results: Llama Dmargin macro-F1 changes from 0.6850 ± 0.02 to 0.7162, and Mistral from 0.6258 ± 0.11 to 0.7087, without explaining the replacement or aggregation. Numerous results are added, including baseline scores, within-party agreement, 16 false positives among 100 audited predictions, and Reddit distributions. The 72 political-label zero-shot scores and existing YouTube prevalence estimates are unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. Engagement, dislike, and positivity measures retain their mathematical meaning; replacing the displayed positivity-ratio formula with prose does not change its definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: an LGBTQ+ hope-speech corpus and classifier, politically associated annotation disagreement, propagation of that disagreement into models, and greater zero-shot alignment with liberal raters. Added analyses support or qualify these contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning within-party diversity, LGBTQ+ experience and contextual recognition, and contrasting rights-based and religious language. It distinguishes community-directed support from general positive sentiment and explains limitations of simplified annotation instructions. The Reddit findings substantively qualify cross-platform generalization by identifying communities where positive comments outnumber negative ones.

D1.justification: v1 promises dataset release upon acceptance; v2 states availability and supplies a repository link. v2 also explicitly documents random selection of Deval from Dseed. Core prompts, software versions, LoRA hyperparameters, A100 hardware, and the approximately 120 GPU-hour disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially develops positioning against sentiment, toxicity, hate-speech, and stance classification, and contextualizes annotation agreement against additional studies. References expand around annotator experience, crowdsourcing, and cross-cultural LGBTQ+ portrayals, while earlier keyword-filtering and infrastructure comparisons disappear. The underlying hope-speech and political-subjectivity positioning remains.

P1.justification: Explanatory passages in Sections 3–5 are extensively revised, with added definitions, synthesis, and limitations discussion. Appendix organization changes substantially: corpus curation moves from F to A, compensation moves from the main text to H, and the original error analysis moves to N. These changes extend beyond adding experimental content.

P2.justification: v2 converts the document to a two-column layout, resizes existing figures and tables, and adds dataset, baseline, demographic, lexical, and supplementary-result tables. Existing video examples and YouTube prevalence results move to Tables A18 and A19. The pipeline and distribution figures retain their content but change placement and scale.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful comparisons, identity analyses, prediction auditing, a concrete qualification of cross-platform generalization, and dataset access information. However, it removes Table 3's standard deviations while replacing scores, assigns 3,105 labels to a stated 250-instance evaluation row in Table 2, and leaves baseline scores and settings in Section 4 versus Table A1 unreconciled. These substantive gains coexist with losses in reporting reliability, preventing a confident net overall quality judgment.
